headline: What to Do If You're Accused of a Drug Crime

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody:
Finding yourself accused of a drug crime can be overwhelming, and it's totally normal to feel a bit lost about what to do next. The legal process can be pretty confusing, but taking the right steps early on can make a big difference in how your case plays out. Your immediate actions are super important for protecting your rights and setting up the strongest possible defense.

First off, remain silent. Seriously, anything you say can and will be used against you, so it's best not to offer explanations or admit to anything without legal advice. Don't resist arrest, even if you think it's unfair; resisting can lead to more charges. As soon as you're able, ask to speak with an attorney. This isn't just a suggestion; it's a critical right you have. Document everything you remember about the arrest, like the time, location, and what was said or done, because these details can be really helpful later on. Lastly, avoid discussing your case with anyone other than your lawyer. This means no social media posts, no talking to friends or family about the specifics, and definitely no speaking with law enforcement without your attorney present. Getting an experienced lawyer involved quickly, like Attorney Angelo Reyes, can help you understand your options and start building a strong defense right from the beginning.
